• In the given sentence, we need to use the conjunction "**even though**".

• It makes the fact in the main clause of the sentence look more **surprising**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

__As I am hearing__ the lecture it reminded me of a book I had read two years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**As I heard** "

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use "**As I heard**" at the beginning to make it the **simple past tense.**
 
• The Past perfect tense is used when out of two actions it is necessary to emphasize that the preceding action was completely finished before the succeeding action started.
 
• There are** two events** in the given sentence. Both are in **past tense **but one is more recent than the other.
 
• The speaker had heard the lecture. This is the **first **event and hence, it takes the simple past tense.
 
• It is followed by remembering the book he had read two years ago. This is the **second **event and hence, it takes the past perfect tense.
 
• The past perfect tense is crucial for putting the events in the sequence in the past.

**The correct sentence is: ***As I heard__ the lecture it reminded me of a book I had read two years ago.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said to him, “May God shower his choicest blessings on you!

options.text: She wished that God might shower his choicest blessings on him.
She wished that may God shower your choicest blessings on Him.
She wished that God might shower his choicest blessings on you.
She wished that God may shower his choicest blessings on you.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**She wished that God might shower His choicest blessings on him**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• There are a few things to keep in mind before changing the sentence from direct to indirect speech.
 
• The reporting verb "**said to him**" changes to "**wished**" as the given sentence is a **prayer **to god for delivering blessings.
 
• The **modal **verb "**may**" changes to "**might**" in indirect speech.
 
• **Modal verbs** express possibility, necessity, and other emotions in indirect speech
 
• The second person pronoun "**you**" changes to "**him**" in the third person pronoun as per the "**object**" of the reporting verb in indirect speech.
 
 
• **Example**: He said to **her**, "*your earings are adorable*"(direct speech)
 
 
• *He told **her **that her earrings were adorable*(indirect speech)
 
 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences which are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. The sectors included agriculture, public health and public utilities among others.

B. The GGI framework covered 10 sectors and 58 Industries.

C. The Good Governance Index (GGI) 2021 scores have been declared.

D. The objective was to provide quantifiable data to compare the performance of different States and Union Territories in these sectors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**CBAD**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the given passage.
 
• **Statement C **is the first sentence of the passage as it delineates the **theme **of the given passage which is the **Good Governance Index (GGI) 2021.**
 
• **Statement B **is the second sentence of the passage as it talks about the **GGI framework covering 10 sectors and 58 Industries**. This is the practical application of the objectives stated in the previous statement.
 
• **Statement A** is the third sentence of the passage as it talks about the** various sectors which are included.** The previous statement ended by talking about different sectors and industries in the GGI framework.
 
• **Statement D** is the last sentence of the passage as the statement begins by stating what the objective was. It was done to provide quantifiable data to compare the performance of different States and Union Territories in these sectors.

Hence, the correct sequence is "**CBAD**"

**The complete passage is:* C****. The Good Governance Index (GGI) 2021 scores have been declared. **B**. The GGI framework covered 10 sectors and 58 Industries. **A**. The sectors included agriculture, public health and public utilities among others. **D**. The objective was to provide quantifiable data to compare the performance of different States and Union Territories in these sectors.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

She is holding free classes for the poor.

options.text: Free classes are being held for the poor by her.
Free classes have been held for the poor by her.
The poor are holding free classes for her.
Free classes are being held by the poor for her.

questions.solution:
The correct sentence is **"****Free classes are being held for the poor by her**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• There are a few things to keep in mind when changing from active to passive voice.
 
• The **object **in the **active voice **becomes the **subject **in the **passive voice **as it comes to the front.
 
• In the given sentence, "**Free classes**" becomes the **subject **in the passive voice.
 
• The **subject **in the active voice becomes the **agent "her" **in the passive voice which comes after the preposition "**by**"
 
• In the passive voice, we use the present participle of 'be' which is "**being**" before the main verb in the sentence that is in the present tense.
 
• In the given sentence, the verb "**holding**" in active voice takes the past participle form "**held**" in the passive voice

**The correct sentence is: ***Free classes are being held for the poor by her.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**
